content: Dual specificity protein phosphatase 1 (DUSP1) is an enzyme encoded by the DUSP1 gene in humans. The expression of the DUSP1 gene is upregulated in human skin fibroblasts in response to oxidative stress, heat stress, and growth factors. The protein encoded by this gene shares structural characteristics with members of the non-receptor-type protein-tyrosine phosphatase family. Additionally, it exhibits significant amino acid sequence similarity to a Tyr/Ser-protein phosphatase encoded by the late gene H1 of the vaccinia virus. The DUSP1 protein, when expressed and purified in bacterial systems, demonstrates intrinsic phosphatase activity. It specifically deactivates mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase in vitro by dephosphorylating both the phosphothreonine and phosphotyrosine residues of MAP kinase. Furthermore, DUSP1 inhibits the activation of MAP kinase by oncogenic Ras in extracts derived from Xenopus oocytes. These findings suggest that DUSP1 plays a critical role in the cellular response to environmental stress and in the negative regulation of cellular proliferation. DUSP1 has been shown to interact with several key proteins, including MAPK14, MAPK1, and MAPK8.
